answer_text:
Let

\[
\Delta_n = a_n-a_{n-1}\qquad (n\ge 1).
\]

The recurrence is

\[
a_{n+1}=\frac{a_n+n a_{n-1}}{n+1},
\]

so

\[
(n+1)a_{n+1}=a_n+n a_{n-1}.
\]

Subtract \((n+1)a_n\) from both sides:

\[
(n+1)(a_{n+1}-a_n)=a_n+n a_{n-1}-(n+1)a_n.
\]

Simplifying the right-hand side gives

\[
(n+1)(a_{n+1}-a_n)=n(a_{n-1}-a_n).
\]

Thus

\[
(n+1)\Delta_{n+1}=-n\Delta_n,
\]

or

\[
\Delta_{n+1}=-\frac{n}{n+1}\Delta_n.
\]

Since

\[
\Delta_1=a_1-a_0=1,
\]

we get

\[
\Delta_2=-\frac12,\qquad
\Delta_3=\frac13,\qquad
\Delta_4=-\frac14,
\]

and in general, by telescoping the product,

\[
\Delta_n=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
a_n=a_0+\sum_{k=1}^n \Delta_k
= \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{(-1)^{k-1}}{k}.
\]

So

\[
a_n=1-\frac12+\frac13-\frac14+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}.
\]

This is the alternating harmonic series, whose limit is

\[
\ln 2.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{\ln 2}
\]
